blockingProblems: SELF-CONTRADICTION, discriminative cooperative networks (para. beginning 'The confusion scheme still needed a sweep'). The scheme is described as 'a guesser that proposes a labelling of the data and a learner trained on whatever the guesser proposes, with the guesser rewarded when the learner reproduces its labels.' As stated this objective is maximized by a constant labelling, which the chapter itself established four sections earlier: 'At c'=a everything is tagged one, the network outputs one everywhere, and performance is perfect by construction.' The chapter therefore asserts, without noticing, that a criterion it already proved degenerate will locate a boundary. Either the anti-collapse ingredient in the actual construction must be stated, or the sentence claims something the chapter has refuted.

MECHANISM MIS-DIAGNOSED, confusion-scheme caveats (para. beginning 'What the peak certifies'). The chapter says the assumption that a classifier 'can resolve the phase and nothing finer' is 'the assumption that fails whenever a network can partly memorize the trial labelling.' Memorization is a finite-sample artifact; the primary and unavoidable reason the idealized W is only idealized is that p(x | parameter) varies smoothly with the parameter *within* a phase, so even a perfectly generalizing classifier beats the piecewise-constant baseline. The chapter then cites Arnold and Schaefer, whose result is explicitly about the infinite-capacity limit where memorization is not the issue and the optimum is a functional of p(x | parameter). The two adjacent sentences give incompatible accounts of why the W deviates from the derivation, and the correct one is left implicit.

MECHANISM ABSENT, closing paragraph of 'When there is nothing to compare against'. Roughly 350 words carrying four separate results (Kottmann et al., Kaeming et al., Huembeli et al.) in a run of 'X then did Y, which produced Z' clauses. Adversarial domain adaptation gets one participial clause with no account of why adapting representations across a parameter region should preserve the phase distinction; influence functions are defined ('quantify how a prediction would shift if a given training sample were reweighted') and then never used in the argument; the factor-of-a-hundred and the 'effective order parameter' are asserted with no indication of what the machine-chosen feature was. This is a citation dump in prose clothing, and it sits directly after the PCA and confusion sections, which are the strongest mechanism-explaining pages in the manuscript. The contrast is what makes it a blocking defect rather than a blemish.

UNRESOLVED TENSION IN THE CLOSING ARGUMENT. The final section asserts that 'Diffusion maps and anomaly detection do not' hand back an interpretable object, 'they return a clustering and a reference distance.' But the chapter had already reported that diffusion maps on the XY model 'clusters samples by winding number' - a named topological invariant. Either the winding-number identification was supplied by the analyst afterwards, in which case say so and the earlier sentence is loose, or the method did return a name, in which case the closing dichotomy is false as stated. The chapter needs one clause here and does not have it.
styleViolations: No em dashes, no '--', no en dashes: clean. No bulleted or numbered lists in the body: clean. No end-of-chapter summary: the final section introduces new material (tensorial-kernel SVMs) and closes on an open problem rather than recapping.

Section heading 'What the covariance matrix knows' against a derivation that is explicitly about uncentered second moments ('the matrix X^T X holds the sample second moments'). The two coincide here only because the column means vanish under Z_2; the chapter never says so, so the heading and the mathematics are describing different objects.

'The same accounting predicts the more interesting case' overstates: the structure-factor argument rationalizes the conserved-order-parameter quartet after the fact, it does not predict the specific cos/sin basis Wang reports.

'A nonlinear autoencoder contains that linear network as a special case' is true only if the activations admit an identity regime; with the sigmoid/ReLU units actually used this is an approximation, not containment. The load-bearing conclusion ('PCA is not a rival but the level they approach from below') survives, but the premise is stated more strongly than it holds.

D_KL is used in the ELBO without the Kullback-Leibler name being spelled out. Borderline, since the subscript is the conventional abbreviation, but the chapter names Eckart-Young, Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, Wolff and Blume-Capel explicitly and is inconsistent here.

Rhetorical ordering implies Wang's label-free PCA came after the confusion scheme ('Lei Wang removed the labels completely', following the van Nieuwenburg section). Wang's preprint predates it by four months. No date is stated in the body so this is not a factual error, but the progression narrative runs against the record.
factProblems: No fabrications found. Every named person, institution-free attribution, venue, volume, page range and DOI in the body and the citation block resolves to a verifiedClaims entry. Checked individually: van Nieuwenburg/Liu/Huber, Arnold/Schaefer, Lei Wang, Hu/Singh/Scalettar, Ce Wang/Zhai, Beach/Golubeva/Melko, Wetzel, Rodriguez-Nieva/Scheurer, Scheurer/Slager, Liu/van Nieuwenburg, Huembeli/Dauphin/Wittek, Huembeli/Dauphin/Wittek/Gogolin, Kottmann/Huembeli/Lewenstein/Acin, Kaeming et al., Greitemann/Liu/Pollet, Greitemann/Liu/Jaubert/Yan/Shannon/Pollet.

All attributed numbers check out against the packet: Kitaev chain ten largest entanglement eigenvalues at L=20 with equal bipartition and mu = -2t; L^2 inputs into L^2 hidden units with two outputs, L=10 finite-size deviation, L=20 giving k_B T_c approx 2.27 J; random-field Heisenberg at L=12 with 64 levels and 10^5 disorder realizations giving h_c approx 3J; blanking window w=3t; Wang's M=1400 from 100 configurations at each of T/J = 1.6 through 2.9, lattice sizes 20^2/40^2/80^2, four degenerate components with cos/sin weights; Wetzel at L=28 (N=784), 50,000 ferromagnetic and 10,000 antiferromagnetic configurations over T in [0,5], 3D XY at L=14, 256-neuron encoder and decoder layers, PCA most accurate and plain autoencoder least.

The corrections array is respected. The Huembeli-Dauphin-Wittek-Gogolin entry is the one live trap - the dossier's original 'post-hoc interpretability tools' description was CORRECTED - and the chapter uses the corrected characterization verbatim in substance: an 'almost entirely unsupervised adversarial game between two networks with conflicting objectives', yielding an effective MBL order parameter, fewer disorder realizations, and roughly a factor of a hundred in numerical effort. Broecker, Ohtsuki and Ohtsuki, Rem et al. and the phantom Nature Physics 2019 landscape article are all absent from the chapter, so none of the other corrected or unverifiable items is repeated.

'Wang states plainly that this quantity was not known to the author before the learner produced it' - packet-supported and correctly hedged as Wang's own statement rather than the chapter's assertion.

Eckart-Young, Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, Wolff, Blume-Capel, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger, Kitaev and Haldane are standard eponyms and are all named where used; no packet entry is required for them and none is missing.
whatWouldMakeItAAA:
"Two of these sections would survive a blind comparison with any monograph in the field. The confusion-curve derivation is done properly - the minority-tag accounting, the check that folding in the far-side samples is an affine map that cannot move the extrema, the asymmetry remark - and the structure-factor section is better than that: the circulant argument, the identification of PCA on a translationally invariant ensemble with diagonalization of the two-point function, and the conclusion that the order parameter is recovered because it is the macroscopically occupied wavevector 'and for no other reason' is the chapter's real contribution, and it is what makes the later Hu-Singh-Scalettar failures land as consequences rather than anecdotes. The Eckart-Young move is equally good: it reframes PCA as the floor the autoencoders approach from below rather than a rival they beat, which turns Wetzel's accuracy ordering into a statement about optimization and identifiability instead of about capacity. Keep all of that untouched.

What drops the chapter below the bar is that the last two sections stop doing the thing the first three do. Four fixes. First, repair the DCN sentence: as written the guesser's objective is maximized by the constant labelling the chapter itself proved gives perfect performance, so state the ingredient that breaks the collapse (what the guesser is a function of, what the learner sees, what forbids a degenerate proposal) or cut the claim. This is not a nitpick - the chapter refutes itself in two sentences separated by four pages. Second, replace 'whenever a network can partly memorize the trial labelling' with the real reason: p(x | parameter) varies within a phase, so a perfectly generalizing infinite-capacity classifier already beats the piecewise-constant baseline, which is precisely why Arnold and Schaefer's optimum is a functional of the distributions and not of phase membership. That single substitution makes the two adjacent paragraphs one argument instead of two incompatible ones. Third, break up the four-paper paragraph in 'When there is nothing to compare against.' Domain adaptation and influence functions each need one sentence of mechanism or should be reduced to a clause; the anomaly-detection material already has its mechanism (the inversion of the burden of proof is the best sentence in the section) and deserves the space the other three are consuming. Fourth, resolve the diffusion-maps tension in the closing argument: say explicitly that the winding-number identification was made by the physicists reading the clusters, not returned by the algorithm, and the closing dichotomy between methods that return a boundary and methods that return a name becomes airtight instead of vulnerable to a reader with a good memory.

Minor but worth doing while the file is open: fix the heading/derivation mismatch on covariance versus second moments with one clause noting the means vanish under Z_2, soften 'contains that linear network as a special case', and spell out Kullback-Leibler once given that every other eponym in the chapter is named."
